text:
eva: Heads-up — saw steady memory creep in kv-cache during long-context replay (~120k tokens). Not OOM, but fragmentation keeps increasing and RSS drifts upward.
perf-bot: perf snapshot: rss 12.1G -> 13.7G over 3h, kv_free_frag=19.7%, alloc_avg_block=3.6KB
marco: Did we try the incremental sampler compactor on that trace? It should reduce free-frag without a big stop-the-world.
eva: Not yet, wanted to gather baseline first. Any quick knobs to experiment before turning on the sampler?
sasha: Two quick ones: raise small-block coalesce threshold and enable async sweep sampling. Also check whether long contexts pin lots of tiny kv entries preventing coalescing.
nate: The avg block ~3.6KB suggests we're over-splitting 16KB slabs into many small pieces. Might be per-slot warmness bias.
marco: Proposed canary config to try:
```
kv.alloc.coalesce_threshold=4KB
kv.compactor.mode=sampling
kv.compactor.sample_rate=0.02
kv.slab.min_split=1KB
kv.slab.tiers=[256B,1KB,4KB,16KB]
```
marco: Sampling compactor will pick ~2% of allocs for incremental coalesce ops to avoid big GC pauses.
perf-bot: note: 0.02 sample_rate on 40k allocs/s ~= 800 coalesce attempts/sec. Watch CPU and lock contention.
eva: Ran single-node canary with that config for 4h. RSS plateaued at 13.0G vs 13.7G baseline. Fragmentation dropped to 11.2%.
sasha: Nice. Any latency impact?
eva: p50 stable, p99 had +4-8ms spikes correlated with coalesce bursts. Traced those to a per-slab lock hold.
nate: Lock contention is expected if coalescer runs inside alloc lock. Consider moving coalesce to background threads with try-lock and time-slicing per slab.
marco: Also think about adaptive sample rate: increase when frag% > 15%, back off when <8%. Eg:
```
base=0.01
if frag > 0.15: sample_rate = min(0.05, base*(frag/0.10))
if frag < 0.08: sample_rate = base
```
marco: This keeps steady-state CPU low and reacts to regressions.
perf-bot: simbed adaptive sampler on synthetic long-context trace: avg CPU +2.7%, frag tightened to 6-9% after 90 minutes.
eva: Good signal. Next canary plan: 1) apply sasha's tiered slabs + min_split=1KB 2) enable adaptive sampler 3) add trace tags to compaction ops (coalesce_duration, slab_id, try_lock_fail) to correlate p99s
sasha: I'll draft short RFC for rollout: include throttle knobs (max_coalesce_ms_per_second, max_ops_per_s) and safe fallback (disable sampler per-node).
nate: +1. Also add a quick console toggle to turn off sampling per-host if latency SLA trips; avoids hotfallback deploys.
eva: Will run that canary tomorrow AM and post logs. One more thought: can we opportunistically coalesce during cold cycles (low request qps) to avoid p99 spikes?
marco: Yes — schedule background coalesces tied to node-load metrics and idle_cpu_pct. If idle>40% -> run at higher sample rate.
ate: Should also consider slight increase to slab size bucket around 8KB for workloads heavy in 1-8KB range. But track internal waste for tiny contexts.
sasha: We'll include histograms in rollout dashboard: alloc histogram, frag%, coalesce ops/sec, p99 latency, cpu%.
eva: Thanks all — I'll post canary summary and raw traces after the run. :thumbsup:
